\chapter{Four Final Forms Before the Verbs}
\label{ch:gu-final-script-closure-a}
\hlchaptermodality{6}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can read and write \gu{ગ}, \gu{એ}, \gu{ખ}, and \gu{ઉ} before the later verb and number lessons use them.}

With every model covered, read \gu{ગ}, \gu{એ}, \gu{ખ}, and \gu{ઉ} and write each one from a spoken sound or role cue, keeping reading and writing scores separate.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[ga]{\gu{ગ} — the consonant ga}

\label{lesson:GU-W06-ga}



\begin{quote}
Write \textbf{\gu{બ}} once from memory. Put it away after one comparison. Today adds one new sound and one new shape: \emph{ga}.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Script — meet one form}
Keep \textbf{\gu{ગ}} visible. Circle the rounded left body to the lower left. Lift once, descend the separate right spine, and turn through its lower foot.

\subsection*{Writing — notice and trace}
Finger-trace \textbf{\gu{ગ}} once, then air-trace it once. Notice rounded body, separate right spine, lower foot; one pen lift.

\subsection*{Writing — copy with the model}
Copy visible \textbf{\gu{ગ}} once. Compare only the body and spine; repair one landmark if needed.

\subsection*{Writing — recall after hiding}
Hide the model and write \emph{ga} once. Uncover \textbf{\gu{ગ}}, compare, and stop after one repair.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Name the sound, the two main landmarks, and the pen-lift count.

Sources: \href{https://www.t30apps.com/gujarati-alphabet-writing/}{Gujarati Alphabet Writing Practice} and the \href{https://www.unicode.org/charts/PDF/U0A80.pdf}{Unicode Gujarati chart}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[e]{\gu{એ} — independent e}

\label{lesson:GU-W06-independent-e}



\begin{quote}
Read \textbf{\gu{ગ}} once, then write independent \textbf{\gu{અ}} once from memory. Say “standing alone,” then put both away. The next independent vowel has its own whole-letter form.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Script — meet one form}
Keep \textbf{\gu{એ}} visible. Circle the left bowl and continue through the lower body and small right arch. Lift once for the full-height right stem and foot. Lift again and sweep the high arc from left to right.

\subsection*{Writing — notice and trace}
Finger-trace \textbf{\gu{એ}} once, then air-trace it once. Notice joined body, separate stem, high arc; two pen lifts.

\subsection*{Writing — copy with the model}
Copy visible \textbf{\gu{એ}} once. Compare only the separate stem and high arc; repair one landmark if needed.

\subsection*{Writing — recall after hiding}
Hide the model and write independent \emph{e} once. Uncover \textbf{\gu{એ}}, compare, and stop after one repair.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Say why this is a whole vowel letter rather than a mark attached to a consonant.

Sources: \href{https://www.t30apps.com/gujarati-alphabet-writing/}{Gujarati Alphabet Writing Practice} and the \href{https://www.unicode.org/charts/PDF/U0A80.pdf}{Unicode Gujarati chart}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[kha]{\gu{ખ} — the consonant kha}

\label{lesson:GU-W06-kha}



\begin{quote}
Write unaspirated \textbf{\gu{ક}} once. Say \emph{ka}. Add a clear puff of air aloud for \emph{kha}, then put the old shape away.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Script — meet one form}
Keep \textbf{\gu{ખ}} visible. Descend through the joined left lobe and curl right through the middle. Lift once, descend the separate right spine, and turn through its lower foot.

\subsection*{Writing — notice and trace}
Finger-trace \textbf{\gu{ખ}} once, then air-trace it once. Notice left lobe, inner curl, separate spine; one pen lift.

\subsection*{Writing — copy with the model}
Copy visible \textbf{\gu{ખ}} once. Compare only the inner curl and right spine; repair one landmark if needed.

\subsection*{Writing — recall after hiding}
Hide the model and write \emph{kha} once. Uncover \textbf{\gu{ખ}}, compare, and stop after one repair.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Read \textbf{\gu{ક} \gu{ખ}} aloud and keep unaspirated \emph{ka} apart from aspirated \emph{kha}.

Sources: \href{https://www.t30apps.com/gujarati-alphabet-writing/}{Gujarati Alphabet Writing Practice} and the \href{https://www.unicode.org/charts/PDF/U0A80.pdf}{Unicode Gujarati chart}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[u]{\gu{ઉ} — independent u}

\label{lesson:GU-W06-independent-u}



\begin{quote}
Write attached short-\emph{u} sign \textbf{\gu{ુ}} once and say “needs a consonant.” Put it away. The same vowel standing alone needs a whole letter.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Script — meet one form}
Keep \textbf{\gu{ઉ}} visible. Circle the small upper bowl to the middle cusp. Continue around the broad lower bowl, then climb the tall outer curve and finish at the upper right without lifting.

\subsection*{Writing — notice and trace}
Finger-trace \textbf{\gu{ઉ}} once, then air-trace it once. Notice upper bowl, middle cusp, lower bowl, outer return; no pen lift.

\subsection*{Writing — copy with the model}
Copy visible \textbf{\gu{ઉ}} once. Compare only the two bowls and outer return; repair one landmark if needed.

\subsection*{Writing — recall after hiding}
Hide the model and write independent \emph{u} once. Uncover \textbf{\gu{ઉ}}, compare, and stop after one repair.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Point to the whole vowel in \textbf{\gu{ઉ} \gu{ુ}}, then point to the attached sign.

Sources: \href{https://www.t30apps.com/gujarati-alphabet-writing/}{Gujarati Alphabet Writing Practice} and the \href{https://www.unicode.org/charts/PDF/U0A80.pdf}{Unicode Gujarati chart}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[ga — independent e — kha — independent u]{\gu{ગ} — \gu{એ} — \gu{ખ} — \gu{ઉ}: four forms return}

\label{lesson:GU-R06-first-four-r1}



\begin{quote}
Keep the four cards visible. Point as you say \emph{ga}, independent \emph{e}, aspirated \emph{kha}, and independent short \emph{u}.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Read the row once from left to right. Name \textbf{\gu{એ}} and \textbf{\gu{ઉ}} as independent vowels. Record a reading score out of four.

\subsection*{Writing — from sound or role}
Cover every model. Write the four cues in order. Record a separate writing score out of four; a reading point cannot replace a written form. Aim for \textbf{4/4} in each column, with one focused repair allowed.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Write the two independent vowels from sound, then name their role.
\end{tcolorbox}
